newsitem.title: FRANCE: Camdessus sees debt relief deals soon.
newsitem.headline: Camdessus sees debt relief deals soon.

text.p: IMF head Michel Camdessus said on Tuesday he expected a decision soon on providing debt relief to a group of countries under an initiative agreed last year.
He cited Uganda, Bolivia, Ivory Coast and Burkina Faso as candidates.
"I think in the next few weeks we will be able to make a decision on a first group of countries," he told reporters after a meeting with French President Jacques Chirac.
The International Monetary Fund, World Bank and Paris Club creditor nations agreed last year to work together on a debt relief initiative to help the world's poor, heavily indebted countries.

Camdessus said that there had been some questions about whether Ivory Coast would qualify for the debt relief initiative since it did not strictly meet criteria for qualification under the initiative.
But he said that he had put forward proposals which would allow Ivory Coast to benefit.
Uganda has long been cited as a likely candidate for early debt relief but France has been pushing to ensure that Ivory Coast, a key ally in west Africa, benefits as well.
